full_judgment: 3. The facts of these suits are that the defendant-petitioners were monthly tenants at the rate of Taka 150 under predecessor of the plaintiff Bank in respect of the northern room of the suit premises named as "Singha Brothers Building" along with a four-roofed tin shed, the schedule of the properties is 0.5 decimals of land of plot No . 749 appertaining to DS khatian No: 1103 under Mouja Hajipur, Upazila Begumgonj. This property was auction sold and purchased by Bath Bank Limited on 6-5-1952 in Money Execution Case No. 6 of 1981 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Noakhali and got delivery of possession on 19-6- 1952. Thereafter, the said Bank converted to Eastern Banking Corporation and thereafter converted to Uttara Bank Limited. After liberation of Bangladesh, the defendant did not pay rents regularly and paid rent up to 1384 BS. Thereafter, they stopped payment of rent and became habitual defaulters. The plaintiff bank requires the suit premises bonafide for opening a new branch at the said premises and the building is required for re-construction and renovation and therefore, the plaintiff terminated the tenancy of the defendant on the expiry of the month of Jaishtha, 1387 BS by serving a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act and asked the defendants to vacate the premises.
